messages.content: Return only JSON matching the supplied schema. Produce a bounded carrier analysis for the Platform Node Inducer's active goal. Authoritative facts: (1) Root AGENTS.md defines root as a Platform Node micro-enterprise whose service is to witness or repair a self-governing Agentic Metro-Enterprise over supplied informational territory; success means the settlement can operate, refuse, transact, attest, amend, and improve with root absent. Root is not capital and must not create a global pool or runtime. Root currently has package identity and historical data but no root-owned content contract, offer, executable, schemas, or conformance fixture. (2) Divination is an existing sovereign settlement with an ActivityStreams solicitation -> provider-authored immutable offer -> capability-bound Accept -> provider-local completion/refusal pattern, digest-linked receipts, seller-local books, EAVT/events, and tests refusing malformed requests and changed terms. Its consideration is internal non-monetary and cannot prove external payment. (3) Stripe Payment Acceptance Enterprise is a separate sovereign emsenn-owned payment rail. It admits only Leader-authorized fixed catalog offerings, creates Stripe Checkout sessions, verifies untouched webhook bytes, uses request/event idempotency, and owns only payment-rail receipts. It never owns the seller's offer, fulfillment, entitlement, customer relationship, or books. Live activation, offering, price, tax, refund terms, beneficiary, payout, and dispute/refund authority remain Leader decisions. (4) Settlement law requires all cross-settlement imports under declared contracts and all writes through the owning settlement's boundary. (5) Current task may build a draft root offer/contract/conformance package and tests, but may not contact customers or activate a live payment offering. Identify precisely what root can reuse as a pattern, what must remain separately contracted, the first artifacts root should own, and what decisions must be reserved for the Leader. Reject a central sales or payment runtime.

reusablePatterns: Divination's solicitation → provider-authored immutable offer → capability-bound Accept → provider-local completion/refusal state machine: root can adopt this sequencing as the canonical offer lifecycle template without owning Divination's implementation.
Digest-linked receipt pattern: each transaction sealed with a content-addressed digest, yielding tamper-evident, verifiable receipts without a central store or runtime.
EAVT append-only event log as the authoritative per-settlement book of record; root can emit root-scoped events in the same shape without touching another settlement's ledger.

Conformance fixture pattern from Divination: tests that reject malformed requests and refuse changed terms prove settlement autonomy; root should author an equivalent suite for its own service boundary.

Stripe's fixed-catalog, Leader-authorized offering model: offerings declared and approved before any activation, never at runtime; root's draft offer schema should follow the same pre-authorization discipline.
Stripe's raw-byte webhook integrity check: verify untouched inbound bytes before acting on any external event; applies to any boundary root will eventually expose.
Request/event idempotency keys on all write operations, making repeated delivery safe without shared state.
separateContracts: Divination settlement boundary: root may declare a named import contract to observe Divination's solicitation pattern, but root must never own, extend, or write into Divination's offer, acceptance state, books, or completion records.

Stripe Payment Acceptance Enterprise boundary: root declares a named import contract for payment-rail access only; Stripe retains exclusive ownership of checkout session creation, webhook verification, price, tax, refund terms, dispute authority, and payment-rail receipts.

Any future sovereign settlement whose artifacts root wishes to observe or cite must be declared under its own named cross-settlement import contract, ratified by the Leader, before any read or write crosses that boundary.
rootOwnedArtifacts: AGENTS.md root charter — already exists; confirms role as witness/repair node, not capital or runtime (no new write needed, but must remain the authoritative constraint source).
Root package identity manifest — already exists; locked version and provenance record.
Historical data corpus — already exists; the informational territory supplied to root.

Draft root content contract: declares root's service boundary (witness/repair of self-governing settlements) and explicitly enumerates what root does not own — capital, global pool, runtime, fulfillment, customer relationship.
Root offer schema: machine-readable, ActivityStreams-compatible document describing the witness/repair service root offers settlements.
Cross-settlement import declaration for Divination: named contract listing which Divination artifacts root may read and under what terms; not activated until Leader ratification.
Cross-settlement import declaration for Stripe: named contract listing the payment-rail surface root may invoke; not activated until Leader ratification.
Root event/receipt schema: shape definitions for root-emitted observations and repair attestations, kept separate from Divination's and Stripe's receipt formats.
Root conformance fixture: test suite asserting that a settlement built with root's artifacts can operate, refuse, transact, attest, amend, and improve with root absent.
Draft test suite rejecting malformed root-service requests and any request to activate a live offering or contact customers.
leaderDecisions: Authorize live activation of any offering on the Stripe payment rail — no activation may occur without explicit Leader sign-off.
Set or approve offering price, tax treatment, and refund terms before any catalog entry is published to any settlement.
Designate beneficiary and payout schedule on the Stripe account; root has no authority to configure or alter these.
Grant or revoke dispute and refund authority; this power never delegates to root or to a settlement by default.
Approve any contact with customers or prospects; the current task boundary explicitly prohibits root-initiated customer contact.
Ratify each cross-settlement import contract (Divination, Stripe, and any future settlement) before root reads or writes across that boundary.
Decide whether Divination's internal non-monetary consideration is sufficient for a given transaction class or whether external Stripe payment is additionally required.
structured_output.firstBuildSlice: Root's first build slice produces the three artifacts it currently lacks: (1) the root content contract — declaring root's service boundary and ruling out capital, global pool, runtime, fulfillment, and customer ownership; (2) the root offer schema — an ActivityStreams-compatible description of the witness/repair service, authored with the same pre-authorization discipline Stripe uses for its fixed catalog; (3) the root conformance fixture — tests asserting a settlement built on root's artifacts can operate, refuse, transact, attest, amend, and improve with root absent. Draft cross-settlement import declarations for Divination and Stripe are written alongside but inert until Leader ratification. No live offering, no customer contact, no payment activation in this slice.
structured_output.principalRisk: Root becomes a covert central runtime by accumulating fulfillment logic, customer state, or payment authority through undeclared cross-settlement reads. Each undeclared dependency erodes settlement autonomy without visibly violating any single rule. Guard: every root artifact must pass the absent-root conformance fixture before merge, and every cross-settlement read must appear in a Leader-ratified import contract before it is exercised.
